packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-08 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / RULES
No proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the four image files of this packet. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
Four images: image-001 = overview of one face (with ruler), image-002 = close tile of it; image-003 = overview of the other face, image-004 = close tile of it. The tiles are small (c. 500 x 720 px).
The fragment is a small irregular scrap of darkened, grey-brown parchment, about 3.5 cm wide by about 5.5 cm high by the ruler, with a diagonal crease or tear line running across it and a jagged torn edge on the text side.
Face A (image-001/002): the left two thirds are blank margin with one or two faint vertical ruling lines (greenish/grey); at the right edge are the first two to three letters of seven lines of a large, formal, upright gothic book hand (textualis, letters roughly 4 mm high, line spacing c. 6-7 mm) in black ink. Line 4 opens with a red capital, about one line high, set at the line head. The lower third of the scrap is blank (lower margin, or text abraded away). So this face preserves a left (outer or inner) margin and line BEGINNINGS.
Face B (image-003/004): mirror situation: the last two to five letters of seven or eight lines at the left edge, then blank margin with vertical ruling to the right. One line end (line 3) has red on or around it - either a red-stroked letter or show-through of the red capital of face A, which sits at the same height (tentative: show-through). So this face preserves line ENDS and a right margin.
No running title, heading, gloss or marginal note is visible in what survives. The crop/scrap does not show whether the page had one or two columns. Tentative interpretation only: the large script module and the one-line red capital are of the kind used for marking verse or sentence openings in a formal book written in large letters; nothing more can be said from the image.

FACE A - line beginnings (image-002, lines counted from the top of the tile)
image-002 line 1: [..](?)[...]        (only the feet of two or three letters at the top edge; possibly "te"/"re" plus a tall letter)
image-002 line 2: tte(?)[...]        (three letters: two t/c-shaped letters and e; could be "cte", "rte" or "ite")
image-002 line 3: te d(?)[...]       (or "re d-", "te o-"; the third letter is a round bowl cut by the tear)
image-002 line 4: [red capital] n(?)[...]      (the red capital has two uprights joined by a crossbar: A or H, possibly N; it is followed by one or two black minims, "n" or "u" or "in")
image-002 line 5: un(?)[...]         (minims only: "un", "nu", "mi", "im")
image-002 line 6: uli(?)[...]        (or "ub-", "ali-"; first letter abraded, crossed by the crease)
image-002 line 7: [.](?)[...]        (faint traces only, under a dark stain)
  -- below: blank / abraded --

FACE B - line ends (image-004, lines counted from the top of the tile)
image-004 line 1: [...](?)           (bottoms of letters only, at the top edge)
image-004 line 2: [...]e(?) suo      (or "-c fuo"/"-e sno"; long s or f, then minims and o)
image-004 line 3: [...]ob(?)         (preceded by a letter cut by the tear, perhaps "x" or "r": "-rob"/"-xob"; b could be h)
image-004 line 4: [...]in(?) iu(?)   (minims, with red over the last group: "-in in", "-m iu", "-ni m"; the red looks like a crossbar and two uprights, i.e. the face-A capital seen through the parchment)
image-004 line 5: [...]temp(us)(?)   (letters "emp" clear enough, followed by a tall stroke or suspension sign, perhaps "temp9"/"tempꝰ"; a preceding letter is cut)
image-004 line 6: [...]ir(?) p(?)    (minim, r or t, then p with a mark above: "-it p'", "-ir p(er)", "-is p")
image-004 line 7: [...]pla(?)        (or "-pta", "-pha"; p, tall letter, a)
image-004 line 8: [...]m(?)[..]      (faint minims, largely lost)
  -- below: blank / abraded --

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
Everything visible was attempted. No connected text survives: face A has only two to three letters at the head of each of seven lines, face B only two to five letters at the end of each of seven or eight lines. No span of ten lines exists on this scrap, and no complete word is certain; the best candidates are "suo" (image-004 line 2) and "temp-" (image-004 line 5).

LIMITATIONS
- Scrap preserves margins plus the extreme edge of the text block only; the lines cannot be joined across faces.
- Parchment is darkened and abraded; the supplied tiles are low resolution (c. 500 px wide), so strokes of this large script are distinguishable but ligatures and abbreviation marks are not secure. A higher-resolution image would help with individual letters but cannot add text.
- Recto/verso order is not determinable.
- Red on face B line 4 may be show-through rather than rubrication.
- Unverified image reading.
